children: Shares of Usana Health Sciences fell after the company lowered its outlook and reported lower revenue in the third quarter.
Shares were down 10% to $13.34 after-hours on Tuesday. The stock closed up 1.2% at $14.87 and had fallen 24% this year through the close.

The multilevel marketer of nutritional and personal-care products on Tuesday said it now expects full-year consolidated net sales of nearly $900 million, down from its earlier guidance for $910 million.
Usana guided for adjusted earnings of 55 cents a share, down from its previous view of 76 cents.
The company reported a loss of $5.6 million, or 30 cents a share, in the quarter ended Oct. 3. That compares with a loss of $6.5 million, or 36 cents a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out certain one-time items, the company reported an adjusted loss of 11 cents a share.
Revenue fell to $205.9 million from $213.7 million a year earlier.

"As we continue our transformation to an omnichannel health and wellness company, our third-quarter results were mixed, with meaningful improvement in some areas and results that fell short of our expectations in others," Chief Executive Kevin Guest said. "We are investing across each of our businesses to strengthen their long-term competitive position and made clear progress in key areas."
